A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same geodesic flow-matching work despite changes to the title and method names. All pages, including appendices, are readable; corresponding equations, algorithms, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-generation and Binarized MNIST experiments, together with sampling, optimizer, and time-conditioning analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original results in Tables 1–4 and its appendices, including translation, MBPP code infilling, and a HumanEval masking experiment.

M1.justification: Logit-FM is renamed KL-flow, with ODE, randomized, and semi-randomized inference renamed basic, sampling, and semi-sampling. Dirichlet initialization, smoothed logit interpolation, marginal denoising loss, and hybrid inference remain. Algorithm 2 makes tokenwise sampling explicit, clarifying the existing marginal approximation rather than establishing a new procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds German-to-English translation using WMT14 and Python code infilling using Python-code/MBPP and TinyCodes/HumanEval. These include both code-only conditioning and function-description prompts. Binarized MNIST image generation is removed. TinyStories and Lamini remain; the English web-text corpus is reported as FineFineWeb instead of the separately cited FineWeb.

E2.justification: Autoregressive models and Gat et al.'s DFM remain the external comparator families. Within corresponding web-text and Lamini comparisons, the ODE/basic variant is removed from Tables 2–3. v2 Table 3 separately evaluates hybrid and sampling inference; v1's row labeled hybrid was described in its text as fully randomized. The additional DFM code-inference budget is a setting variation.

E3.justification: v2 reports 1.5B, 52-layer, width-1536 models for complex tasks, replacing v1's stated 12-layer, width-768 configuration, and adds a 150M comparison. Conditional evaluation changes from averaged responses to Top-5 and Avg reporting. New code protocols introduce line/token masking, compilation and unit-test metrics, and DFM budgets of N versus 3N steps. Lamini's combined 512-token length was already stated in v1.

E4.justification: v2 adds a model-size comparison and a HumanEval sensitivity analysis across masking probabilities from 0.1 to 0.8. Existing top-k, learning-rate/optimizer, time-conditioning, and hybrid-switch analyses are retained in Figures 3–7, largely through relocation. ODE comparison rows disappear from the web-text and Lamini evaluations, but the central existing ablation questions remain represented.

E5.justification: v1 Section 4.3 explicitly averages eight independent response-generation runs per instruction. v2 Section 5.3 replaces this with best-of-five and average response reporting. This concerns sampled responses, not independently trained models. Neither version reports confidence intervals, seed-based variability, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Web-text and Lamini results are substantially replaced, and translation and code results are added. At 1024 NFE, Table 2 changes from hybrid Llama 2 perplexity 54.5 on FineWeb to 35.1 and 32.7 for 150M and 1.5B models on FineFineWeb; these are different-setting results. Lamini's reported leading method changes from autoregressive to hybrid under revised evaluation. MNIST FID results disappear, while TinyStories Table 1 and the retained appendix curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The numbered definition, propositions, and corollary largely reorganize v1's existing interpolation and marginal-expectation derivation. However, v2 Equations 11–12 insert a 1/(1-t) loss factor absent from the corresponding v1 equations, and Section 3.2 explicitly asserts product-marginal exactness at t=1. These are limited mathematical revisions; no convergence proof for the empirical sampler is added.

C1.justification: The geodesic and likelihood contributions remain, but the headline empirical claims expand to translation and code infilling. v2 newly claims that DFM fails at one inference step per missing code token and becomes impractical when three times as many steps are needed. Its conclusion replaces v1's sweeping autoregressive-superiority statement with task-specific claims about sampling and hybrid inference.

C2.justification: v1 favors fully randomized inference for Lamini. v2 instead interprets hybrid inference as preferable when instructions admit multiple valid responses, while sampling suits more deterministic translation. It also adds scaling expectations and code-infilling applicability constraints. However, Appendix D retains v1's recommendation of t*=0 for Lamini, leaving the revised main-text interpretation unreconciled.

D1.justification: v2 adds model-size specifications, Python training-data access information, code filtering and masking instructions, and autoregressive infilling formatting. Appendix A specifies 200,000 training iterations, batch size 40, and training/output length limits. Existing hardware, modded-GPT access, optimizer guidance, and time-conditioning details remain; image-model specifications are removed. The additions are concrete but localized.

R1.justification: v2 adds references associated with MBPP, WMT14, and FineFineWeb, while removing the MNIST and original FineWeb references. It introduces a task-specific critique of DFM's code-infilling efficiency. The broader flow-matching and diffusion positioning is retained, with much of the existing literature review moved to Appendix E.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, background, theoretical exposition, experimental narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Discrete-sequence methodology becomes a separate section with single-token and sequence cases. Related work is shortened in the main text, and existing top-k and literature discussions move into an expanded appendix structure. This substantially reorganizes retained content.

P2.justification: v2 adds a three-panel method overview, a code-results table, and a HumanEval figure, while removing the MNIST figure. Table 2 gains model-size information, and Table 3 gains dataset groups and Top-5/Avg subcolumns. Existing analysis figures are relocated and resized, including the formerly full-width top-k figure.

improvement.justification: Translation and unit-tested code infilling provide more informative evidence about practical conditional generation than v1's instruction benchmark alone. The model-size comparison, method overview, and additional protocol details also improve assessability. These gains are limited by the unreconciled Lamini recommendation in Appendix D and inconsistent LFM/DFM model naming in Appendix A. Changed corpora and configurations also prevent treating revised scores as same-setting performance improvements.
